title: DECISION: deterministic mailbox IDs via SHA-256(uid_le || role)
description: Special-use mailbox IDs are derived as SHA-256(user_id as 8-byte little-endian || role as UTF-8), taking the first 16 bytes, base32-encoded without padding (26 chars). The algorithm is documented with an independent Python oracle. This means the ID is stable across database restores, computable without a DB round-trip, and collision-resistant for all practical purposes. Alternative rejected: auto-increment primary key as mailbox ID. That would change if the database were restored from a backup or migrated, breaking any client-cached JMAP mailbox IDs. Alternative rejected: random UUID at creation time. That is stable but requires a DB read before any operation can verify the ID is legitimate. Tradeoff: the derivation must be documented and tested against an external oracle (done), and the little-endian byte order is a fixed commitment.
